No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । अमेरिकाको भर्जिनियास्थित अदालतमा ममता काफ्ले भट्ट हत्या मुद्दाको अन्तिम बहस चलिरहेको थियो । न्यायाधीश र निर्णायक मण्डलसामु उभिएकी सरकारी वकिल सारा सामीले एकपछि अर्को प्रमाण प्रस्तुत गरिरहेकी थिइन् । उनको निशाना थिए- ममताका श्रीमान् नरेश भट्ट । करिब ४७ मिनेट लामो बहसको अन्त्यतिर भने उनको स्वरमा एउटा फरक भाव देखियो । उनले अब केवल अपराधका प्रमाण र नरेशका झुटबारे कुरा गरिनन्, ममताको परिवारले भोग्नुपर्ने कहिल्यै नमेटिने पीडाको चित्र पनि कोरिन् । उनले निर्णायक मण्डललाई भनिन्, ‘नरेशलाई ममताको अन्तिम सम्झनासमेत नियन्त्रण गर्न नदिनुहोस् । उनलाई त्यसो गर्न नदिनुहोस् ।’ सामीले ममताको शव अहिलेसम्म नभेटिएको प्रसंग उठाउँदै परिवारले छोरीको अन्तिम संस्कारसमेत गर्न नपाउने पीडा सम्झाइन् । ‘लुरे, भर्जिनियाको ल्यान्डफिल नै ममताको अन्तिम विश्रामस्थल बनाइएको छ । उनको परिवारका लागि ममता सधैँ हराइरहनेछिन् । उनीहरूलाई उनको अन्तिम संस्कार गर्ने अवसर कहिल्यै मिल्ने छैन । उनका अवशेष कतै फोहोरको थुप्रोमुनि थिचिएका छन्,’ उनको भनाइ थियो । उनले यसाे भनिरहँदा इजलासमा गहिराे स्तब्धता छाएकाे थियाे । ममताका आमा, दाइ र शुभचिन्तकहरू भक्कानिएका थिए । यो केवल एउटी महिलाको हत्या मुद्दा थिएन । एउटी छोरी, श्रीमती, आमा र परिवारकी सदस्यको जीवन कसरी अन्त्य भयो भन्ने प्रश्नसँगै उनको अस्तित्वसमेत मेटाउने प्रयास भएको अभियोजन पक्षको तर्क थियो । सामीले आफ्नो बहसको सुरुवात नरेशले ममतालाई पठाएको एउटा सन्देशबाट गरेकी थिइन् । नरेशले ममतालाई लेखेका थिए, ‘The days are coming that you will regret a lot.’ अर्थात्, अब तिमीले धेरै पछुताउनुपर्ने दिन आउँदैछन् । सामीका अनुसार यो सन्देश ममता हराउनुभन्दा १६२ दिनअघि पठाइएको थियो । उनले निर्णायक मण्डलसमक्ष भनिन्, ‘१६२ दिनपछि उनले आफ्नो वाचा पूरा गरे । १६२ दिनपछि नरेशले ममताको हत्या गरे । उनको शरीर टुक्राटुक्रा पारे र फोहोरसरह फालिदिए ।’ उनले यो सन्देशलाई नरेशको नियत र घटनाबीचको महत्त्वपूर्ण कडीका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरिन् । सामीले ममता र नरेशको वैवाहिक सम्बन्धलाई सामान्य पारिवारिक विवादका रूपमा मात्र हेर्न नहुने तर्क गरिन् । उनका अनुसार नरेशले ममताको फोन प्रयोगमा रोक लगाएका थिए, आर्थिक पहुँच नियन्त्रण गरेका थिए र उनलाई गाडी प्रयोग गर्नसमेत कठिन बनाएका थिए । ममताले आफ्ना श्रीमानलाई घरमा ‘राजा’ भनेर सम्बोधन गर्ने गरेको प्रसंगलाई समेत सामीले आफ्नो बहसमा जोडिन् । तर उनको व्याख्यामा त्यो राजाको घर प्रेम र सुरक्षाको घर थिएन । ‘वास्तविकता के थियो भने ममता त्रासको घरमा बाँचिरहेकी थिइन् । नरेशसँग त्यो यातनाको साम्राज्य थियो, जहाँ उनी राजा बनेर शासन गर्थे,’ सामीको भनाइ थियो । उनले नरेशलाई ‘मास्टर म्यानिपुलेटर’ अर्थात् अरूलाई आफ्नो नियन्त्रणमा राख्न र भ्रमित पार्न माहिर व्यक्ति तथा झुटको मालिकका रूपमा चित्रण गरिन् । ‘आत्महत्या गरेको भए प्रहरीलाई किन बोलाएनन् ?’ अदालतमा नरेशले ममता मृत अवस्थामा भेटिएको र उनले विष सेवन गरेर आत्महत्या गरेको दाबी गरेका थिए । आफूले करिब ४५ मिनेटदेखि एक घण्टासम्म उनलाई बचाउने प्रयास गरेको तर डर र त्रासका कारण प्रहरीलाई खबर गर्न नसकेको उनको भनाइ थियो । तर शवलाई आरा र चक्कुको प्रयोग गरी टुक्र्याएको तथा फोहोरमा फालेको कुरा उनले स्वीकार गरेका थिए । सामीले यही स्वीकारोक्तिलाई नरेशको कथामाथि प्रश्न उठाउने आधार बनाइन् । ‘उनले ममताको शरीर टुक्राटुक्रा पारे, फोहोरको कन्टेनरमा हाले, तर उनको मृत्युमा आफ्नो कुनै भूमिका छैन भन्ने विश्वास हामीलाई गराउन खोजिरहेका छन् । यो हास्यास्पद छ,’ उनले भनिन् । उनले घटनास्थलमा भेटिएको रगतको प्रमाण, सरसफाइका सामग्री, आरा खरिद गरेको विवरण, सीसीटीभी फुटेज र नरेशका विभिन्न बयानबीचको विरोधाभासलाई पनि निर्णायक मण्डलसमक्ष राखिन् । ममता हराएको खबर सन् २०२४ को अगस्टमा सार्वजनिक भएको थियो । त्यसपछि सुरु भएको अनुसन्धानले नरेशमाथि शंका बढाउँदै लग्यो । ममताको शव भने अहिलेसम्म फेला परेको छैन । करिब दुई वर्षभन्दा लामो प्रतीक्षापछि सुरु भएको मुद्दामा झन्डै छ हप्तासम्म बहस र साक्षीका बयान चले । अन्ततः नोभेम्बर १० मा निर्णायक मण्डलले नरेशलाई प्रथम श्रेणीको हत्यासहित शव लुकाएको र शवको अपमान गरेको तीनवटै अभियोगमा दोषी ठहर गर्‍यो । निर्णय सार्वजनिक हुँदा नरेश अदालतमा शान्त देखिएका थिए । उनकाे अनुहारमा आत्मग्लानीकाे कुनै पनि भाव थिएन । तर ममताका परिवार र शुभचिन्तकका लागि त्यो क्षण लामो प्रतीक्षापछिको एउटा महत्त्वपूर्ण क्षण बन्यो । नरेशले सजायस्वरूप आजीवन कारावाससम्म भोग्नुपर्ने हुन सक्छ । उनको सजाय निर्धारण सन् २०२७ मार्च १२ मा हुने तय भएको छ । The final arguments in the Mamta Kafle Bhatt murder case were underway in a court in Virginia, USA. Standing before the judge and jury, public prosecutor Sara Sami was presenting evidence one after another. Her target was - Mamata's husband Naresh Bhatt. Towards the end of the nearly 47-minute debate, however, a different tone emerged in her voice. She no longer just talked about the evidence of the crime and Naresh's lies, but also painted a picture of the unending pain that Mamata's family must endure. She told the jury, "Don't let Naresh control even Mamata's last memory. Don't let him do that." Sami mentioned the fact that Mamata's body has not been found yet, and the pain of the family not being able to even perform their daughter's last rites. "The landfill in Luray, Virginia, has become Mamata's final resting place. Mamata will forever be lost to her family. They will never have the opportunity to give her a last rites. Her remains are buried under a pile of garbage somewhere," he said. As he spoke, there was a deep sense of shock in the courtroom. Mamata's mother, brother and well-wishers were stunned. This was not just a case of the murder of a woman. The prosecution argued that it was an attempt to erase the existence of a daughter, wife, mother and family member, along with the question of how her life ended. Sami began her argument with a message that Naresh had sent to Mamata. Naresh had written to Mamata, 'The days are coming that you will regret a lot.' That is, the days are coming when you will have to regret a lot. According to Sami, this message was sent 162 days before Mamata disappeared. She told the jury, "After 162 days, he fulfilled his promise. After 162 days, Naresh murdered Mamata. He dismembered her body and threw it away like garbage." She presented this message as an important link between the king's intentions and the events. Sami argued that Mamata and Naresh's marital relationship should not be viewed as just a normal family dispute. According to him, Naresh had banned Mamata's phone use, controlled her financial access, and even made it difficult for her to use a car. Sami also added to her argument the incident of Mamata addressing her husband as 'King' at home. But in his interpretation, that king's house was not a house of love and security. "The reality was that Mamata was living in a house of terror. Naresh had an empire of torture, where he ruled as king," Sami said. She portrayed Naresh as a 'master manipulator', a person skilled at controlling and misleading others, and a master of lies. "If he committed suicide, why didn't they call the police?" In court, Naresh claimed that Mamata was found dead and that she had committed suicide by consuming poison. He said that he tried to save her for about 45 minutes to an hour, but could not inform the police due to fear and panic. But he admitted to dismembering the body using a saw and knife and throwing it in the trash. Sami used this confession as the basis for questioning Naresh's story. "They dismembered Mamata's body, threw it in a garbage container, but they are trying to make us believe that they had no role in her death. This is ridiculous," she said. She also presented to the jury the contradictions between the blood evidence found at the scene, cleaning supplies, details of the purchase of the saw, CCTV footage, and various statements by Naresh. The news of Mamata's disappearance was made public in August 2024. The investigation that began thereafter increased suspicions against Naresh. Mamata's body has not been found yet. The trial, which began after a wait of more than two years, lasted nearly six weeks of arguments and witness testimony. Finally, on November 10, the jury found Naresh guilty of all three charges, including first-degree murder, concealment of a body, and desecration of a corpse. Naresh appeared calm in court as the verdict was announced. There was no trace of self-blame on his face. But for Mamata's family and well-wishers, the moment was a momentous one after a long wait. Naresh could face up to life in prison as a punishment. His sentencing is scheduled for March 12, 2027.

Standing before the judge and jury, public prosecutor Sara Sami was presenting evidence one after another. Her target was - Mamata's husband Naresh Bhatt. Towards the end of the nearly 47-minute debate, however, a different tone emerged in her voice. She no longer just talked about the evidence of the crime and Naresh's lies, but also painted a picture of the unending pain that Mamata's family must endure. She told the jury, "Don't let Naresh control even Mamata's last memory. Don't let him do that." Sami mentioned the fact that Mamata's body has not been found yet, and the pain of the family not being able to even perform their daughter's last rites. "The landfill in Luray, Virginia, has become Mamata's final resting place. Mamata will forever be lost to her family. They will never have the opportunity to give her a last rites. Her remains are buried under a pile of garbage somewhere," he said. As he spoke, there was a deep sense of shock in the courtroom. Mamata's mother, brother and well-wishers were stunned. This was not just a case of the murder of a woman. The prosecution argued that it was an attempt to erase the existence of a daughter, wife, mother and family member, along with the question of how her life ended. Sami began her argument with a message that Naresh had sent to Mamata. Naresh had written to Mamata, 'The days are coming that you will regret a lot.' That is, the days are coming when you will have to regret a lot. According to Sami, this message was sent 162 days before Mamata disappeared. She told the jury, "After 162 days, he fulfilled his promise. After 162 days, Naresh murdered Mamata. He dismembered her body and threw it away like garbage." She presented this message as an important link between the king's intentions and the events. Sami argued that Mamata and Naresh's marital relationship should not be viewed as just a normal family dispute. According to him, Naresh had banned Mamata's phone use, controlled her financial access, and even made it difficult for her to use a car. Sami also added to her argument the incident of Mamata addressing her husband as 'King' at home. But in his interpretation, that king's house was not a house of love and security. "The reality was that Mamata was living in a house of terror. Naresh had an empire of torture, where he ruled as king," Sami said. She portrayed Naresh as a 'master manipulator', a person skilled at controlling and misleading others, and a master of lies. "If he committed suicide, why didn't they call the police?" In court, Naresh claimed that Mamata was found dead and that she had committed suicide by consuming poison. He said that he tried to save her for about 45 minutes to an hour, but could not inform the police due to fear and panic. But he admitted to dismembering the body using a saw and knife and throwing it in the trash. Sami used this confession as the basis for questioning Naresh's story. "They dismembered Mamata's body, threw it in a garbage container, but they are trying to make us believe that they had no role in her death. This is ridiculous," she said. She also presented to the jury the contradictions between the blood evidence found at the scene, cleaning supplies, details of the purchase of the saw, CCTV footage, and various statements by Naresh. The trial, which began after a wait of more than two years, lasted nearly six weeks of arguments and witness testimony. Finally, on November 10, the jury found Naresh guilty of all three charges, including first-degree murder, concealment of a body, and desecration of a corpse. Naresh appeared calm in court as the verdict was announced. There was no trace of self-blame on his face. But for Mamata's family and well-wishers, the moment was a momentous one after a long wait. Naresh could face up to life in prison as a punishment. His sentencing is scheduled for March 12, 2027.

The final arguments in the Mamta Kafle Bhatt murder case were underway in a court in Virginia, USA. Standing before the judge and jury, public prosecutor Sara Sami was presenting evidence one after another. Her target was - Mamata's husband Naresh Bhatt. Towards the end of the nearly 47-minute debate, however, a different tone emerged in her voice. She no longer just talked about the evidence of the crime and Naresh's lies, but also painted a picture of the unending pain that Mamata's family must endure. She told the jury, "Don't let Naresh control even Mamata's last memory. Don't let him do that." Sami mentioned the fact that Mamata's body has not been found yet, and the pain of the family not being able to even perform their daughter's last rites. "The landfill in Luray, Virginia, has become Mamata's final resting place. Mamata will forever be lost to her family. They will never have the opportunity to give her a last rites. Her remains are buried under a pile of garbage somewhere," he said. As he spoke, there was a deep sense of shock in the courtroom. Mamata's mother, brother and well-wishers were stunned. This was not just a case of the murder of a woman. The prosecution argued that it was an attempt to erase the existence of a daughter, wife, mother and family member, along with the question of how her life ended. Sami began her argument with a message that Naresh had sent to Mamata. Naresh had written to Mamata, 'The days are coming that you will regret a lot.' That is, the days are coming when you will have to regret a lot. According to Sami, this message was sent 162 days before Mamata disappeared. She told the jury, "After 162 days, he fulfilled his promise. After 162 days, Naresh murdered Mamata. He dismembered her body and threw it away like garbage." She presented this message as an important link between the king's intentions and the events. Sami argued that Mamata and Naresh's marital relationship should not be viewed as just a normal family dispute. According to him, Naresh had banned Mamata's phone use, controlled her financial access, and even made it difficult for her to use a car. Sami also added to her argument the incident of Mamata addressing her husband as 'King' at home. But in his interpretation, that king's house was not a house of love and security. "The reality was that Mamata was living in a house of terror. Naresh had an empire of torture, where he ruled as king," Sami said. In court, Naresh claimed that Mamata was found dead and that she had committed suicide by consuming poison. He said that he tried to save her for about 45 minutes to an hour, but could not inform the police due to fear and panic. But he admitted to dismembering the body using a saw and knife and throwing it in the trash. Sami used this confession as the basis for questioning Naresh's story. सामीले आफ्नो बहसको सुरुवात नरेशले ममतालाई पठाएको एउटा सन्देशबाट गरेकी थिइन् ।

नरेशले ममतालाई लेखेका थिए, ‘The days are coming that you will regret a lot.’

अर्थात्, अब तिमीले धेरै पछुताउनुपर्ने दिन आउँदैछन् ।

सामीका अनुसार यो सन्देश ममता हराउनुभन्दा १६२ दिनअघि पठाइएको थियो ।

उनले निर्णायक मण्डलसमक्ष भनिन्, ‘१६२ दिनपछि उनले आफ्नो वाचा पूरा गरे । १६२ दिनपछि नरेशले ममताको हत्या गरे । उनको शरीर टुक्राटुक्रा पारे र फोहोरसरह फालिदिए ।’

उनले यो सन्देशलाई नरेशको नियत र घटनाबीचको महत्त्वपूर्ण कडीका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरिन् ।

सामीले ममता र नरेशको वैवाहिक सम्बन्धलाई सामान्य पारिवारिक विवादका रूपमा मात्र हेर्न नहुने तर्क गरिन् ।

उनका अनुसार नरेशले ममताको फोन प्रयोगमा रोक लगाएका थिए, आर्थिक पहुँच नियन्त्रण गरेका थिए र उनलाई गाडी प्रयोग गर्नसमेत कठिन बनाएका थिए ।

ममताले आफ्ना श्रीमानलाई घरमा ‘राजा’ भनेर सम्बोधन गर्ने गरेको प्रसंगलाई समेत सामीले आफ्नो बहसमा जोडिन् ।

तर उनको व्याख्यामा त्यो राजाको घर प्रेम र सुरक्षाको घर थिएन ।

‘वास्तविकता के थियो भने ममता त्रासको घरमा बाँचिरहेकी थिइन् । नरेशसँग त्यो यातनाको साम्राज्य थियो, जहाँ उनी राजा बनेर शासन गर्थे,’ सामीको भनाइ थियो ।

उनले नरेशलाई ‘मास्टर म्यानिपुलेटर’ अर्थात् अरूलाई आफ्नो नियन्त्रणमा राख्न र भ्रमित पार्न माहिर व्यक्ति तथा झुटको मालिकका रूपमा चित्रण गरिन् ।

‘आत्महत्या गरेको भए प्रहरीलाई किन बोलाएनन् ?’

अदालतमा नरेशले ममता मृत अवस्थामा भेटिएको र उनले विष सेवन गरेर आत्महत्या गरेको दाबी गरेका थिए । आफूले करिब ४५ मिनेटदेखि एक घण्टासम्म उनलाई बचाउने प्रयास गरेको तर डर र त्रासका कारण प्रहरीलाई खबर गर्न नसकेको उनको भनाइ थियो ।

तर शवलाई आरा र चक्कुको प्रयोग गरी टुक्र्याएको तथा फोहोरमा फालेको कुरा उनले स्वीकार गरेका थिए ।

सामीले यही स्वीकारोक्तिलाई नरेशको कथामाथि प्रश्न उठाउने आधार बनाइन् ।

‘उनले ममताको शरीर टुक्राटुक्रा पारे, फोहोरको कन्टेनरमा हाले, तर उनको मृत्युमा आफ्नो कुनै भूमिका छैन भन्ने विश्वास हामीलाई गराउन खोजिरहेका छन् । यो हास्यास्पद छ,’ उनले भनिन् ।

उनले घटनास्थलमा भेटिएको रगतको प्रमाण, सरसफाइका सामग्री, आरा खरिद गरेको विवरण, सीसीटीभी फुटेज र नरेशका विभिन्न बयानबीचको विरोधाभासलाई पनि निर्णायक मण्डलसमक्ष राखिन् ।

ममता हराएको खबर सन् २०२४ को अगस्टमा सार्वजनिक भएको थियो । त्यसपछि सुरु भएको अनुसन्धानले नरेशमाथि शंका बढाउँदै लग्यो । ममताको शव भने अहिलेसम्म फेला परेको छैन ।

करिब दुई वर्षभन्दा लामो प्रतीक्षापछि सुरु भएको मुद्दामा झन्डै छ हप्तासम्म बहस र साक्षीका बयान चले । अन्ततः नोभेम्बर १० मा निर्णायक मण्डलले नरेशलाई प्रथम श्रेणीको हत्यासहित शव लुकाएको र शवको अपमान गरेको तीनवटै अभियोगमा दोषी ठहर गर्‍यो ।

निर्णय सार्वजनिक हुँदा नरेश अदालतमा शान्त देखिएका थिए । उनकाे अनुहारमा आत्मग्लानीकाे कुनै पनि भाव थिएन । तर ममताका परिवार र शुभचिन्तकका लागि त्यो क्षण लामो प्रतीक्षापछिको एउटा महत्त्वपूर्ण क्षण बन्यो ।

नरेशले सजायस्वरूप आजीवन कारावाससम्म भोग्नुपर्ने हुन सक्छ । उनको सजाय निर्धारण सन् २०२७ मार्च १२ मा हुने तय भएको छ ।

But he admitted to dismembering the body using a saw and knife and throwing it in the trash. Sami used this confession as the basis for questioning Naresh's story. "They dismembered Mamata's body, threw it in a garbage container, but they are trying to make us believe that they had no role in her death. This is ridiculous," she said. She also presented to the jury the contradictions between the blood evidence found at the scene, cleaning supplies, details of the purchase of the saw, CCTV footage, and various statements by Naresh. Finally, on November 10, the jury found Naresh guilty of all three charges, including first-degree murder, concealment of a body, and desecration of a corpse. Naresh appeared calm in court as the verdict was announced. There was no trace of self-blame on his face. But for Mamata's family and well-wishers, the moment was a momentous one after a long wait. Naresh could face up to life in prison as a punishment. His sentencing is scheduled for March 12, 2027.
